title: Three legend rows still name keys their editor never answers (needs per-face keymap modes)
body:
## Summary
The ads take grid draws V 'inspector view' and the trailer cut draws A 'adopt · pick' and V 'inspector view' in their Keycaps legends, and neither editor registers those verbs.

## Description
AdsTakesEditor (app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Takes.tsx) shares mode part.frames with the frames board, whose V cycles the inspector's unit/alternatives/review views; the ads face has no inspector views and registers only item, next-missing, render, adopt. TrailerEditor (app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Trailer.tsx) shares part.script with the script board (adopt, view) and registers only item and deselect. PartWorkspace draws keyTable(mode, facts) (packages/ui/src/components/part/PartWorkspace.tsx:83), so these rows are dead controls (video-assembly gap-and-refusal-honesty). The in-scope half (CutFinish, ScoreBed, the two take grids' facts) landed in 0f94256b; the rest needs a mode per face in packages/ui/src/keymap/bindings.ts (e.g. part.frames.takes with J/K, N, enter, 1-9; part.script.trailer with J/K, Esc) or a legend filter by registered verbs, which is outside this context.

## Flow
- open an ads project's frames part: the legend's V row does nothing
- open a trailer's script part, select a beat: A and V rows do nothing
- fix: add the two face modes to bindings.ts and switch the two editors to them; extend the legend diff in part-editor-media.test.ts to both

## Expected impact
A keyboard user stops pressing keys the legend offers and nothing answers. Could break: a binding conflict check in packages/ui/test on the new modes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the legend equals the keys the dispatcher answers on every media editor
Before: 3 dead rows (AdsTakes V; Trailer A, V), measured by the legend diff in tests/next-server/part-editor-media.test.ts applied to these two editors
After: 0 dead rows (predicted)
Method: simulation - the instrument exists and reads 3 dead rows; the fix is in packages/ui/src/keymap/bindings.ts, another context's path
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: packages/ui/src/keymap/bindings.ts:190 (part.script adopt/view), :207 (part.frames view); app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Takes.tsx useKeys part.frames verbs item,next-missing,render,adopt; Trailer.tsx useKeys part.script verbs item,deselect
instrument: tests/next-server/part-editor-media.test.ts legend() diff extended to AdsTakesEditor (full rows) and TrailerEditor

title: A frames layer row is a role=button no key can press, with a button nested inside it
body:
## Summary
The layers list in FramesInspector selects a layer on click only; its div carries role=button and tabIndex=0 but no key handler, and it nests the show/hide Button.

## Description
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/FramesInspector.tsx:144 renders <div role="button" tabIndex={0} onClick=...> with no onKeyDown, so Enter and Space on a focused row do nothing (WAI-ARIA button pattern requires both), and the row contains <Button label=hide|show> - an interactive inside an interactive. Fixed looks like a real <button> for the select with the hide button as its sibling, or Enter/Space handled - but Enter is also part.frames' render key and the keymap's target rules decide which wins, which only a DOM run can show.

## Flow
- Tab to a layer row in the frames inspector
- press Space or Enter -> nothing selects (Enter may reach the render receipt instead)
- fix: split the row into a select button and the hide button; keep aria-pressed on the select

## Expected impact
Keyboard and screen-reader users can select a layer to nudge or reorder; today only a pointer can. Could break: the canvas's layer selection sync.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a layer row is operable by keyboard
Before: 0 of 2 activation keys work on 1 role=button row; 1 nested interactive
After: 2 of 2; 0 nested (predicted)
Method: simulation - no DOM in the node lane, and the keymap's Enter handling on a focused control is what decides the build
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a live or jsdom probe: focus a layer row, press Space/Enter, assert the layer is selected and the render receipt did not open; axe nested-interactive count

title: The ad's finish checks lose their target, so loudness shows a number with no -14 LUFS beside it
body:
## Summary
lib/cut/ads/finish.ts gives every ad check a target (-14 LUFS for loudness), the part view drops it, and CutFinish draws a second spelling of the finish row without one.

## Description
adFinishChecks returns target on each row (lib/cut/ads/finish.ts:98, :170 `-14 LUFS`); app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureCut.ts:190 maps checks without target, and AdFinishData.checks (packages/domain/src/partView.finish.ts:181) has no target field. CutFinish (app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/CutFinish.tsx:121-128) re-implements the check row Cut.tsx's FinishRows draws as `value / target`. The video-assembly doctrine 'loudness is delivered to a number' wants the measured value and its target side by side. Fixed: carry target through the domain type and both port sides, and render the ad's checks through FinishRows.

## Flow
- render an ad aspect so loudness reports
- the checks inspector reads e.g. '-13.2 LUFS  pass' with no target
- fix: add target to AdFinishData.checks, map it in fixtureCut and the real side, draw FinishRows in CutFinish

## Expected impact
The operator reads loudness against its delivery number, and the timeline and the ad share one finish row. Could break: parts-finish/parts-verdict fixtures that snapshot the checks.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every finish check renders its target; one finish-row renderer
Before: 5 ad checks rendered with 0 targets; 2 finish-row renderers
After: 5 of 5 targets; 1 renderer (predicted)
Method: simulation - the domain type and both port sides are part-port-real-and-contract's paths
Result: better
Gate: contract
instrument: a parts-finish case asserting each ad check carries target, plus the part-editor-media harness reading the finish inspector rows

title: Playback re-renders the whole cut and score editors on every display frame
body:
## Summary
useTransport sets React state on every requestAnimationFrame, so the Timeline and Spotting editors - PartWorkspace, rail, inspector and every lane block - re-render at 60-120 Hz while playing.

## Description
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/CutClock.tsx useTransport: the frame loop calls setT(next) each frame; Cut.tsx Timeline and Score.tsx Spotting hold tr.t, so each frame re-renders the editor and CutClock recomputes median(scenes) (a sort) and re-maps every block. The registry's motion performance-discipline ('frames bypass reactive state'; 'anything re-rendering at frame rate is routed through the wrong layer') names this. Fixed: the needle and the timecode read the clock through a ref-driven subscription (or a small store via useSyncExternalStore scoped to the needle and readout), and the editor renders only on seek/play/pause.

## Flow
- open a cut with 30 scenes, press Space
- React devtools: Timeline renders ~60/s
- fix: move t out of editor state; only Needle and Readout subscribe

## Expected impact
Smoother playback on long cuts and less CPU on the operator's box. Could break: the auto-scroll-to-needle effect and the monitor's scene lookup, which read t.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - editor renders per second of playback
Before: ~1 Timeline render per display frame (60/s at 60 Hz), by reading: setT per rAF tick
After: renders only on transport events; needle moves via the subscribed child (predicted)
Method: simulation - render counting needs the harness to count Timeline calls over a stubbed frame loop; not built this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/CutClock.tsx useTransport step(): setT(next) per frame; Cut.tsx:132 and Score.tsx:109 hold tr.t
instrument: hook harness counting Timeline/Spotting function calls over 1 s of stubbed rAF at 60 Hz (before ~60, after ~0)

title: Most write buttons in the media editors stay pressable while a write is in flight
body:
## Summary
12 of 17 single-op buttons (accept, discard, revert pass, rederive, accept row, revert row, remove text, add text, hide/show, clear motion, reset beat) draw enabled while busy; PartEditor drops their press silently.

## Description
PartEditor's write() declines a second op while one is in flight (inflight ref), so a press on these buttons does nothing and says nothing; their key twins return false when busy (Frames.tsx order/hide/accept, Motion accept) and 5 already take disabled={busy} (Cut -50 ms, +50 ms, snap; Score add cue, delete cue; Motion accept and ScoreTakes use do too). Fixed: disabled={busy} on every op button, the same rule the keys follow.

## Flow
- press accept in the frames proposal bar, then discard before it answers
- discard does nothing, drawn enabled
- fix: thread busy into the remaining 12 buttons

## Expected impact
The operator sees which controls are waiting instead of pressing dead ones. Could break: nothing measurable beyond the disabled look.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - write buttons disabled while a write is in flight
Before: 5 of 17 single-line op buttons disabled while busy (grep over 13 editor files)
After: 17 of 17 (predicted)
Method: probe - grep count; the per-button behaviour needs the harness walk to pin it
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Frames.tsx:134,200,208-210; FramesInspector.tsx:91,96,118,134,147; Motion.tsx:117; Trailer.tsx:97 (no disabled); Cut.tsx:110-114, Score.tsx:81,181 (disabled)
instrument: part-editor-media harness: render each editor with busy=true and count op Buttons whose disabled is not true (before 12, after 0)
